thread.title: Apple May Be Bruised in U.S.-China Trade War

author: Barron's
title: Apple May Be Bruised in U.S.-China Trade War
text:
Bloomberg News Apple ( AAPL ) has bet, and invested, big in China. Nearly one-fifth of its fiscal year revenue ($44.7 billion) came from the region. It shipped more than 41 million iPhones in that same time. And it has about 40 stores in the country.
So when President Donald Trump threatened additional tariffs late Monday on $200 billion worth of Chinese goods, and China's Commerce Ministry promised countermeasures, it left the most-valued company in the U.S. exposed. [On Friday, the White House announced tariffs of 25% on up to $50 billion in Chinese goods, including semiconductors. Apple depends greatly on Asian suppliers such as Taiwanese firm Foxconn Technology (Taiwan: 2354), where iPhones are assembled.]
Tim Bajarin , president of market researcher Creative Strategies , tells Barron's that tariffs could impact Apple at some point. "Both countries are playing a game of brinkmanship or bluff and neither want to give in," he says. "All tech companies need to be aware of this possibility."
Neil Campling , co-head of global thematic group at Mirabaud Securities , is more blunt. He told CNBC , "Apple is most exposed."
While Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook has received assurances from Trump that iPhones built in China would not be affected by tariffs, Apple could be at serious risk if China clamps down on its suppliers. There also is the outside chance Beijing recommends citizens bypass the iPhone and buy smartphones produced by Chinese vendors like Huawei Technologies and ZTE (China: 000063).
Apple's exposure is the most severe among the so-called Faang companies because of its commitment to China.
Facebook ( FB ) is blocked in China, and Netflix ( NFLX ) and Amazon.com ( AMZN ) have minimal presences. Alphabet ( GOOGL ) Google's search function is blocked in the country although it has a presence in China through the Android operating system.
"We continue to strongly believe that, given the primarily services nature of traditional Faang names and very internationally distributed from a revenue perspective with China representing negligible revenue/growth, that Facebook, Amazon, Netflix, and Google/Alphabet are'primarily insulated' from tariff worries and a potential retaliatory trade war with China if negotiations fail to result in a path to an agreement over the coming weeks," Daniel Ives, head of technology research at GBH Insights , wrote in a note to clients Tuesday.
